text:
Frank Nazar told the Daily Herald that fixing Chicago's slide starts with him, and he's now been moved to the wing, per Chicago Hockey Now. He has 5 goals and 7 points in 16 games, including two goals in one period against Florida.

Our numbers say he's been one of the unluckiest players in the league. Chicago has scored 11.4 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, and that's costing him assists. His own finishing is fine, 5 goals on 4.9 expected. The Blackhawks get 44% of the expected goals at five on five with him on, almost five points better than without him, which on this team is a quiet win.

Evolving-Hockey's note from last season is that he plays with some of the weakest teammates in the league, which drags his raw numbers down. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has him carrying the puck in on 62% of his entries and getting to the home-plate area at the 83rd percentile. Watch his assist total: when the team's finishing around him recovers, his points should come with it.
headline: Frank Nazar deserves more than seven points
